titre_page: How to make a menu with buttons, a switch and a slider in Yop2D? | Yop2D Guide
description: Build a real menu in Yop2D: buttons of every shape, switch, checkbox, slider, panel and counter, no code. Change the shape, colors, image and sound from one place.
h1: How to make a menu with buttons, a switch and a slider?
carte: A full menu: buttons, switch, slider, all set in one place.
etapes: Tap + then "Interface elements" and pick a button.
Inspector > "Element style…": shape, colors, image, text.
A formula reads =name.progression for a switch or a slider.
blocs: A game menu needs good-looking buttons and settings: a switch for the sound, a slider for the volume, a counter for the score. In Yop2D, every element is **a single object** with its text inside, and its whole look is set in one window. You can also download the **UI kit** example (Examples tab): it shows every element.
a project open in the editor;
the "UI kit" example if you want to see the result first (optional).
Tap the **+** of the editor, then the **Interface elements** section.
The element arrives in the middle of the screen: move it with your finger and resize it with the handles, like any object.
The text of a button is inside it: write it in the Inspector, no need to place a text on top of the button anymore.
Select the element and tap **Element style…** in the Inspector.
In **Shape**, choose rectangle, rounded, pill, circle, cut corners or hexagon.
In **Image**, choose **Inside the shape** (the image keeps the shape), **Replaces the shape** (the image IS the button) or **Icon + text**.
In **Colors and outline**, set the color, the **gradient**, the outline, the **shadow** and the **glow (neon)**.
In **Text**, choose the font, the size, the color and the outline of the letters.
In **Behavior**, turn on **Stays pressed (ON / OFF)** for a button that keeps its state.
Choose a **sound on touch** and, if you like, a **vibration**.
For a slider, set the **minimum value**, the **maximum value** and the **starting value**.
A **disabled (greyed)** element no longer reacts to touch: handy for a "Continue" button that is not available yet.
Step 4: read the value in the game
A switch or a checkbox equals its minimum value (off) or maximum value (on); a slider equals its position.
In a formula, write **object_name.progression**: for example "=volume.progression" in [[modifier_propriete]] of a text to display the volume.
For a button, add the event [[NoeudEventClicObjet]] in the Blueprint and choose your button.
The old Yop2D buttons keep working: these new elements are added, they replace nothing.
